subject: social
topic: Social media usage correlates with increased loneliness despite higher digital connectivity
angle: While social media addiction and problematic use are linked to loneliness and depression, active use is linked to greater online support and wellbeing.
title: The Connectivity Paradox

hooks.text: Is your social media making you feel alone?
You think social media isolates you. The evidence shows active use can provide support.
You are scrolling because you are lonely.
A thumb swipes over a glowing screen in a silent room.

reveal.headline: Active social media use is linked to greater online support.
reveal.body: While problematic use correlates with loneliness, active engagement is linked to better wellbeing and support.

explain.headline: The evidence on social media is mixed.
explain.body: Problematic use correlates with depression and loneliness. However, active use is linked to positive affect and support. Most findings are correlational.

matters.headline: The way you use the screen matters.
matters.body: That may be why some people find community while others feel isolated. It is not just the time spent, but the nature of the interaction.

example.headline: A late night scroll.
example.body: You sit in a dark room. The blue light hits your face. You move from one profile to the next, looking for a connection that feels distant.

question.headline: Are you seeking connection or just escaping it?

stat.label: daily limit that may lead to significant well-being improvement

claims.text: Active social media use is linked to greater online support (r = .34), wellbeing (r = .15), positive affect (r = .11), and symptoms of anxiety (r = .12).
claims.quote: between-person associations for active SMU and greater online support (r = .34), wellbeing (r = .15), positive affect (r = .11), and symptoms of anxiety (r = .12)

claims.text: Passive social media use is linked to greater online support (r = .15).
claims.quote: passive SMU and greater online support (r = .15)

claims.text: Limiting social media use to approximately 30 minutes per day may lead to significant improvement in well-being.
claims.quote: Our findings strongly suggest that limiting social media use to approximately 30 minutes per day may lead to significant improvement in well-being.

claims.text: Problematic social media use is linked to moderate correlations with depression and loneliness.
claims.quote: The mean correlations of problematic SM use with life satisfaction and self-esteem are small, whereas those of problematic SM use with depression and loneliness are moderate.

verdict: The evidence shows that while problematic and addictive social media use correlates with loneliness and distress, active engagement can be linked to positive outcomes like online support.
caveat: Most findings are correlational, with the exception of one experiment suggesting that limiting use may reduce loneliness.
caption:
Social media usage and loneliness have a complex relationship.

Research shows that while problematic use correlates with depression, active engagement is linked to online support. Most findings remain correlational.
